claims.text: The starting material is HfZrTiTa0.53 with a quasi-static yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
The starting material has a quasi-static compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
The starting material has a quasi-static fracture strain of approximately 13.5%.
A brief thermomechanical treatment followed by rapid quenching can generate a dispersed nanoscale precipitate population in the target alloy.
The treatment will produce approximately 3–5 vol% precipitates.
The precipitates produced in HfZrTiTa0.53 will be ductile BCC particles.
The nanoscale BCC precipitates will be uniformly distributed within the primary matrix.
The precipitates will act as barriers to dislocation motion.
The precipitates will serve as sources for dislocation multiplication.
Impeded dislocation glide and increased dislocation multiplication will enhance strain hardening.
Enhanced strain hardening will delay shear-band formation and strain localization under high-rate adiabatic compression.
The treated alloy will have a dynamic yield strength exceeding 786 MPa at strain rates of approximately 10^2–10^3 s^-1.
The treated alloy will sustain more than 13.5% strain before localization or fracture under dynamic compression.
The treatment will improve resistance to shear localization relative to untreated HfZrTiTa0.53 tested under the same dynamic conditions.
More spatially distributed plastic deformation will increase impact-energy absorption.
More spatially distributed plastic deformation will reduce impact-induced energy release.
The prediction is limited to adiabatic compressive loading at strain rates of approximately 10^2–10^3 s^-1.

Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in dynamic yield strength, deformation before localization, and impact-energy absorption versus an identically tested untreated control would falsify the hypothesis.
